ranked_evidence.title: Thakur (title) - Wikipedia
ranked_evidence.snippet: # Thakur (title). **Thakur** (Anglicized as **Tagore**) is a historical feudal title of the Indian subcontinent. The female variant of the title is **Thakurani** or **Thakurain**, and is also used to describe the wife of a Thakur. It is viewed to have been derived from word *Thakkura* which, according to several scholars, was not an original word of the Sanskrit language but a borrowed word in the Indian lexis from the Tukharistan region of Uzbekistan. In India, this title is widely used by the people belonging to the Rajput community while few people of other communities also use this title include communities such as, Bengali Brahmins, Bhumihars, Charans and Kolis. The meaning of the word *Thakur* was suggested to be "god" by S. He doubted, however, that *Thakkura* is "an original Sanskrit word" and was of the opinion that *Thakkura* is probably a loan word from the Prakrit language.
